Q: Call Outlook procedure using VBScript A:

To kick off your procedure in Outlook 365, you can use the procedure below. Be sure to create a Task in Outlook for this to work. Place all code in "ThisOutlookSession". It will kick off your macro and NOT show the Reminder; essentially a silent processing of your Outlook macro.

Private Sub Application_Reminder(ByVal Item As Object)

Set olRemind = Outlook.Reminders

If TypeName(Item) = "TaskItem" Then
    Dim myItem As TaskItem
    Set myItem = Item
    If myItem.Subject = "run macro YourMacroName" Then

        Call YourMacroName    '...your macro name here
       
    End If
End If
End Sub

Private Sub olRemind_BeforeReminderShow(Cancel As Boolean)

    Dim objRem As Object 

    For Each objRem In olRemind
        'Note:  Caption should be same as "Subject" in Application_Reminder above
        If objRem.Caption = "run macro YourMacroName" Then
            If objRem.IsVisible Then
                objRem.Dismiss
                Cancel = True
            End If
            Exit For
        End If
    Next objRem

End Sub

Q: MySQL use GROUP_CONCAT as a condition A:

Here's a solution:

SELECT 
    b.name,
    GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT p.number) product_numbers,
    COUNT(DISTINCT a.product_code) AS addon_count
FROM box b
LEFT JOIN product p ON p.box_ident = b.ident
LEFT JOIN addons a ON p.number = a.product_code
GROUP BY b.ident;

This extra join does expand the number of rows of the pre-aggregated result, but the fact that both aggregation functions are using DISTINCT compensates for this in this case. Keep this in mind in the future if you use it in queries that aren't using DISTINCT in aggregation.

The addon_count doesn't really count addons, it counts how many products in a given box have at least one addon. That seems to be what your query would have done if it worked.

Demo: https://dbfiddle.uk/9-T9ICkb

Your query wouldn't work for a couple of reasons:

  • GROUP_CONCAT() returns a string with comma-separated values, not a list that can be used in the IN() predicate.
  • An expression in the select-list can't refer to an alias created by another expression in the same select-list. Also, the order of which expression is evaluated first is not defined, so you can't depend on product_numbers being filled before the subquery is evaluated anyway.

Q: I really want to learn Rust. please help me A:

Rust is intended to support data structures like that (it's a general purpose systems programming language, you should be able to write anything in it and make it performant to boot), but they functionally require working with raw pointers, which is harder to get right (and requires unsafe code, making it riskier because it now relies on humans to guarantee safety through analysis), so the standard library does it for you. Many language safety rules mean that you can't implement the common data structures without what would otherwise be considered non-idiomatic code.

For example, std::vector in C++ maintains a dynamically allocated array of raw bytes under the hood that's typically larger than needed to hold the currently stored elements, and uses explicit placement new and manual destructor calls to populate and clear it. The whole design is a hack to improve performance and reduce the requirements on types, and it's all technically legal standard C++, aside from the fact that it typically uses an implementation-defined C++ equivalent to C's realloc for resizing, which a user-defined type doesn't have access to (they'd have to write their own allocator from scratch to allow potential in-place reallocs, or use C's memory allocation routines and hope they never need to interact with C++ memory allocation).

Rust is the same way, but moreso. Yes, you could technically construct a doubly-linked list from Rces and RefCells, maybe tacking on Weak as well if you want to avoid the whole thing being cyclic references, and other awfulness without writing any unsafe code, but it's hard to get correct, and it's less performant. So we delve into non-idiomatic realms of Rust and use unsafe raw pointers (but deeply encapsulated to minimize the amount of actual unsafe code required). It's all standards-compliant, it's just ugly. The user sees none of this complexity, they just get to use a full safe interface.

Q: PHP MySQL - select where id not equal to two one of 2 ids A:

Use NOT IN. You're also missing the call to prepare().

$statment = $db ->prepare("SELECT * FROM player
                    WHERE id NOT IN (?, ?)
                    ORDER BY RAND()
                    LIMIT 2");

Also, the order of clauses in a SELECT statement is:

SELECT
FROM
JOIN
WHERE
GROUP BY
HAVING
ORDER BY
LIMIT
